title: GPU Architecture Graduate Intern
description:
Job Details:
Job Description:
The Role and Impact
As a Silicon Architecture Graduate Intern, you will contribute to the definition and architecture of cutting-edge silicon solutions, including hardware, firmware, and platform specifications. You will assist in modeling and simulation to analyze performance, power, and feature trade-offs across interconnected subsystems, guiding architectural decisions to meet product goals. In this role, you will collaborate with architects, design engineers, and validation teams to support the early-stage feasibility and specification development of innovative technologies.
Business Group
You will be part of the Data Center Group (DCG), a global organization dedicated to powering the world's digital infrastructure. The team focuses on developing highly scalable and efficient solutions to support Intel's leadership in advanced computing and data center technologies. Joining this group provides the opportunity to contribute to Intel's broader mission of enabling continued innovation in high-performance computing and data solutions.
Key Responsibilities
- Assist in defining silicon architecture specifications based on product requirements and feature integration.
- Support modeling and simulation tasks to evaluate performance, power, and trade-offs for architectural decisions.
- Collaborate with architects, design engineers, and validation teams to ensure feasibility and alignment with product goals.
- Contribute to the development of high-level models and tools for architectural analysis.
- Explore GPU concepts such as SIMT, parallelism, and cache hierarchies to guide architectural improvements.
- Apply programming skills in C, C++, and Python for prototyping and analysis tasks.
Qualifications:
Minimum Qualifications
- Pursuing master's degree in GPU architecture, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering or tightly related field.
- Knowledge of GPU architecture concepts, including SIMT, parallelism, and cache hierarchies.
- Proficiency in C, C++, and Python programming.
- Understanding of hardware pipelines and basic RTL design methodologies.
- 3.0 GPA
Preferred Qualifications
- Strong problem-solving and analytical skills to address complex technical challenges.
- Excellent communication and teamwork abilities to thrive in a collaborative environment.
- Enthusiasm to learn and grow within Intel's innovative ecosystem, contributing to impactful technologies.
Ready to launch your career in silicon architecture? Join us to gain hands-on experience, expand your skills, and make an impact in shaping the future of computing technologies.
